title: Meta prepares Hatch agent and Watermelon model with a $199.99 premium tier
subtitle: The consumer agent is designed to drive bookings on DoorDash, Etsy, Reddit, Yelp and Outlook, paired with a new flagship model and a subscription that puts Meta directly against OpenAI's ChatGPT Pro and Anthropic's Max.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Meta is in final stages of rolling out Hatch, a consumer AI-agent platform, alongside a new flagship model internally called Watermelon, according to reports from The Decoder, PYMNTS and Yahoo Finance circulating October 1–2. Hatch is a direct consumer version of OpenClaw. It is designed to execute tasks on third-party sites — DoorDash, Etsy, Reddit, Yelp and Outlook are the named integrations — and to offer a customizable dashboard that stitches in modules like fitness tracking and trip planning. Meta is weighing a tiered price structure topping out at $199.99 per month. Watermelon is reported to use roughly ten times the training compute of its predecessor Muse Spark and to reach GPT-5.5 parity on Meta's internal benchmarks. Those numbers have not been independently verified.

The shift here is the business model, not the capability. Meta's AI products have historically been free, ad-supported, and bundled into the social apps. A $199.99 subscription is the same tier as ChatGPT Pro and Claude Max. It signals that Meta believes consumer agents are a willingness-to-pay market, not an engagement-driver for Instagram and WhatsApp. The integration list is the other tell: DoorDash and Etsy and Yelp are commerce surfaces where an agent making bookings on your behalf converts directly to transaction revenue, so Meta can plausibly take a cut on top of the subscription.

The frontier right now has three distinct consumer-agent plays: OpenAI's Dots, which lives inside ChatGPT and keeps working after you stop chatting; Anthropic's Claude agents, which lean enterprise and developer; and Meta's Hatch, which is explicitly a commerce-adjacent butler. If Watermelon's internal numbers hold under outside testing, it also narrows the capability gap Meta has had with the frontier labs since late 2024. If they don't, the subscription price will be the first thing to compress.

For learners: watch the integrations more than the model. Agent products succeed or fail on what they can reliably book, buy, and send on your behalf — not on benchmark scores. If you want to understand where consumer AI is actually going, pick one of Hatch's listed integrations, open its API docs, and read what an agent can and cannot do through it. That is the real surface where the next year of competition plays out.
